name: Intraosseous Venous Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiologic Diagnostic Criteria for Intraosseous Venous Malformation

criteria.description: Presence of well-defined, radiolucent, multilocular lesion with characteristic 'soap bubble' or 'honeycomb' appearance on imaging
Histological confirmation showing dilated, thin-walled venous channels within bone
Localized swelling or deformity of affected bone with or without pain
No evidence of malignant transformation or aggressive bone destruction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus characteristic radiologic features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging and histopathology; clinical features support but are not definitive alone.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized bony swelling with palpable venous channels
searchTerms: bony lump with visible venous channels

pathognomonic.symptomName: Radiologic multilocular radiolucent lesion with honeycomb pattern

common.symptomName: Soft tissue swelling adjacent to affected bone
Intermittent bleeding or hemorrhage from lesion site

occasional.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to nerve compression
occasional.notes: If lesion is near neural foramina

occasional.symptomName: Localized warmth or erythema overlying lesion
Mild functional impairment of affected limb or region

rare.symptomName: High-output cardiac failure secondary to large arteriovenous shunting
searchTerms: heart failure from abnormal blood flow
heart problems due to blood vessel shunts

laboratory: Normal blood counts unless hemorrhage or secondary infection present
imaging: X-ray showing multilocular radiolucent lesion with honeycomb or soap bubble appearance
MRI demonstrating venous channels with slow flow and absence of arterial feeders
CT scan showing cortical thinning and bone expansion
genetic: No known consistent genetic mutations identified
other: Histopathology revealing dilated, thin-walled venous channels within bone trabeculae

distinguishingFeatures: Intraosseous hemangiomas often show more trabecular thickening and less venous channel predominance
Hemangiomas may have a more cavernous vascular pattern on histology
Aneurysmal bone cysts present with blood-filled cystic spaces and rapid expansion
Histology shows blood-filled spaces without endothelial lining
Fibrous dysplasia shows ground-glass radiographic appearance
Histology reveals fibrous stroma with irregular woven bone trabeculae

redFlags: Severe localized pain unresponsive to analgesics
references: Nakashima M, et al. Intraosseous venous malformations: clinical and radiologic features. Skeletal Radiol. 2018.
Dubois J, et al. Vascular anomalies: classification, diagnosis, and treatment. Springer, 2014.
